experiment: Collecting the law into one rulebook
result: 2,470 pieces from 22 norms at 4 levels (Spain, Catalonia, metropolitan area, Barcelona).
decision: One file, data/rulebook.jsonl, is the only source of legal text for every later stage.

experiment: Testing 9 rules on real flats
result: 32% of Swiss flats and 38% of ResPlan plans pass every rule. 97 of 341 shops pass the rules an empty shell can meet.
decision: The rules work on real data; the generator must pass all 9 before a plan is shown as "works".

experiment: Cleaning the shop dataset
result: 180 of 341 shops kept.
decision: The generator and every later test use these 180 shops (data/clean/nomad_shells.json).

experiment: Learning room sizes from flats that pass
result: Typical (median) and compact (25th percentile) sizes for studio, 1-, 2- and 3-bedroom flats.
decision: The generator uses these learned sizes; "compact rooms" in Grasshopper switches to the smaller set.

experiment: First plan generator: flats along the façade
result: With "as many flats as fit", 144 of 180 shops get a working proposal, 360 flats in total.
decision: Stage 6 v2 must add patios (PGM art. 225.7), back flats and a shared corridor.

experiment: Reading a plan drawing
result: With one known size given: outline overlap 0.93 (1 = perfect), area within 10% on 77% of plans. Without a size the reader's own scale guess is 54% off.
decision: Reader v1 is in NOMAD.gh: Plan file + known_facade_m + read plan.

experiment: GitHub scan and a plan-reader race
result: On messy plans: ours 83% area within 10%, MitUNet 63%, dark lines alone 87%, AI model alone 72%.
decision: Keep our reader. Next tests need real scanned plans (CubiCasa5K) where AI should matter. Stage 5–7 start from the repos marked Use / Copy the method.

experiment: Flags on the plan, drawn in Rhino
result: Asking 2 × 1-bed + 1 × 2-bed: 40 shops YES, 105 PARTLY, 43 NO. The card that fails most is 'Flats that fit' (146 shops): the shop runs out of façade or depth. 26 shops have more than 20% of their floor dark.
decision: Stage 5 v1 lives in NOMAD.gh. The daylight part stays as it is (Bars owns the daylight analysis). Next: Stage 6, better plans.

experiment: Before and after: the smallest change that houses more flats
result: Asking 2 × 1-bed + 1 × 2-bed of all 180 shops: shops where everything works 40 → 43; flats that pass 251 → 266. Asking 5 × 1-bed + 2 × 2-bed: flats that pass 306 → 347.
decision: Stage 6 v2 is in NOMAD.gh (the 3D shows the after plan; patios light blue, corridor grey). Next: new windows in blind street walls (needs cadastre data on which walls face the street) and Stage 7, the 3D model.

experiment: The demo: from a commercial plan to homes, in Rhino
result: All 180 shops, asked 2 × 1-bed + 1 × 2-bed. Stage 5 as it is: 41 YES, 104 PARTLY, 43 NO. Homes: iteration 1 266, iteration 2 304, iteration 3 466 (YES in 154 shops; at least one home in 157 shops).
decision: This is what we show. Next: new windows in blind walls (cadastre data), Bars's daylight analysis, and IFC / glTF export of the Stage 7 models.

experiment: From zoning to walls: doors and windows in Rhino
result: All five demo shops built: for the large shop, iteration 3 has 12 homes, 32 windows, 12 entries; every layout shows its rooms, halls and openings.
decision: Stage 7 is now two steps: 7.1 zoning, 7.2 walls, doors, windows. Next: check door widths and the hall turning circle against the rules, then IFC export.

experiment: Zoning: can each empty shop in Barcelona become housing at all?
result: 5,026 of 6,149 empty premises (82 %) stand in a zone that admits housing on the ground floor (13a 2,334, 12 1,383, 13b 1,259, 15 49); 817 depend on their zone's own plan; 306 do not (facilities, parks, industry, port). In the Eixample: 1,160 of 1,224 (95 %).
decision: Zoning is NOMAD's first gate (step 3, now running). Next: the inner-block condition of art. 225.7, and the 817 'check' premises against their detailed plans.

experiment: Rule cards and a golden set: does NOMAD use the right numbers?
result: Before the fixes: 12 of 16 right (3 rules not checked; 2,50 m used where a shop conversion needs 2,40 m; one article wrong). After: 16 of 16, every citation right. Keyword search finds the right article first for 13 of 16 questions and in the top 5 for 15.
decision: Three checks added (living room on the façade >= 2,20 m, wet rooms >= 2,20 m high, hall >= 1 m), 2,40 m for conversions, art. 323 cited for zone 13. Re-score the golden set after every rule change.

experiment: The 3D as IFC and glTF: the model leaves Rhino
result: 12 IFC + 12 glTF files for the demo shops (results/model3d/); the IFC files pass IfcOpenShell's schema check with 0 problems. The largest: 497 walls, 26 windows, 48 doors, 60 rooms.
decision: Stage 7 is complete. Next: open the IFC in a BIM viewer with the team, and the glTF in a web page.

experiment: The plan reader on 398 real scanned plans
result: On 398 real scans: dark lines only 0.71 median overlap (26 % of areas within 10 %); ours 0.69 (20 %); MitUNet 0.68 (19 %); the AI model alone 0.61 (19 %). On our own drawings the same reader scored 0.93 (77 %).
decision: Keep asking for one size and showing what was found so the user can correct it. Next: fine-tune the wall model on scans (CubiCasa's train split), and test on CVC-FP (122 scans from the UAB, Barcelona).

experiment: NOMAD on Barcelona's real empty shops
result: 5,688 of 6,056 premises kept after cleaning; NOMAD ran on 1,694. As they are: 155 YES, 946 PARTLY, 593 NO; after the smallest change 225 YES. Up to 2,855 homes fit, in 1,192 shops.
decision: Real shops are now the main test set. Next: the Catastro CAT file (src/building/cat_file.py, ready) to cut shared floors into each shop.

experiment: The website: owner mode, plan upload, three languages, report
result: The same answer as Rhino in about 12 s in the browser. Plan upload traces clean drawings; on a scanned plan the tracer fails and the click-the-corners mode is needed.
decision: Publish; the uploaded-plan reader moves to the fine-tuned model when it beats dark lines.

experiment: Fine-tuning the plan reader on real scans
result: On the 40 check scans the wall overlap rose from 0.098 to 0.118. On the 398 test scans it got worse: outline overlap 0.617 (published model 0.685, dark lines 0.709), area within 10 % on 11 % (published 20 %, dark lines 26 %).
decision: Keep the published weights. A real fine-tune needs the full train split (about 4,000 scans) and a longer run; the download is the bottleneck (about 1-2 scans a minute).

experiment: The rulebook as one book: the original official PDFs
result: 1,408 pages, 54 MB (the 117 MB B1600 scan re-encoded to greyscale). Online: 26 files under 11 MB each. All 17 rules located; 13 with highlighted paragraphs (the 4 on scanned pages open at the right page).
decision: The flipbook is the rulebook's public face; the search viewer stays for the team.

experiment: Bars's daylight model on Barcelona's real empty shops
result: 1,650 shops: median predicted daylight factor 1.2 %; 420 well lit (>= 2 %), 858 some daylight, 372 dark (< 1 %). Median lit depth 2.95 m (our fixed assumption was 5.5 m). On the 111 shops Bars also modelled, geometry agrees within centimetres and the predicted DF median 1.15 % vs his 1.12 %. Only 211 shops are fully inside his training ranges.
decision: Show Bars's prediction with every real shop (map card, Design homes, Grasshopper component 7) and use DF < 1 % as 'not liveable' in the avoid answer. More simulations at wider ranges would make it firmer.

experiment: 'Avoid' as an answer: which shops should not become homes
result: 896 candidates, 714 not liveable, 565 keep it a shop (4 or fewer shops within 100 m; city median 16), 306 not allowed, 3,668 not modelled yet (mostly shared ground floors).
decision: New map mode on the website: 'NOMAD's answer, with avoid'. The 10 % cut is a design choice to discuss with the team.

experiment: NOMAD.gh split into small components
result: 10 components, 0 errors; the report shows zoning, Bars's daylight (DF 3.3 %), the before / after verdict and every rule card.
decision: The old single component stays in grasshopper/archive.

experiment: Iterations as circulation strategies (Finch-style)
result: Real shops: most homes 497 -> 379, homes as asked 333 -> 261, floor in homes 27 % -> 33 %. Test shops: 466 -> 421, 266 -> 248, 42 % -> 54 %. The old 'most homes' plans had 59 (real) and 19 (test) flats lit only by a patio.
decision: plan2 strategies replace the patio iterations in Rhino and on the website.

experiment: What makes a flat habitable: 13,444 real plans measured
result: Circulation 12 % of the flat, hall 1.75 m wide; front door into a hall (85 %) from a common stair or corridor; living and bedrooms on the façade (95 %); flats reach 6 m from the window. NOMAD's plans: circulation 16 %, hall 1.10 m, kitchen 1.6 m and 2nd bedroom 2.2 m wide, 34 % of the shop floor left unused, every flat entered from the street.
decision: Rebuild the flat layout on these rules (docs/habitability_rules.md) before anything else.

experiment: Real flats, stretched to fit: a plan library, a plan graph and door clearances (Finch's method)
result: 920 real flats NOMAD can use (51 studios, 290 one-beds, 454 two-beds, 125 three-beds); fits score 77-98. On 40 real Barcelona shops: 54 legal homes in 28 shops (old generator: 70 homes in 28 shops, with narrower invented rooms).
decision: plan3 replaces plan2 in Rhino and on the website; the library is the source of every flat plan.

experiment: The building's own stair, ResPlan, door swings, a plan gallery and weight sliders
result: Street library: 761 real flats that pass every rule incl. door swings (575 Swiss Dwellings, 186 ResPlan; 390 two-beds). 40 real shops: 52 legal homes in 28 shops. Engine 1-2 s per shop in the browser.
decision: Keep the strict door rules (they are the law); add second lobbies for long façades next.

experiment: A street door for every street façade, and the 25 m rule for every flat
result: 40 real shops: 53 legal homes in 28 shops; a 1,479 m² shop gets 8 homes off 4 street doors. The large demo shop drops from 8 to 6 homes: two of its earlier flats were more than 25 m from the street door.
decision: Keep: every flat within 25 m of a street door; one door per 40 m of street façade.

experiment: Furniture, your own plans, generated plans and an assistant (the rest of the Finch list)
result: 690 of 761 real street flats can be furnished as the law asks. 40 real shops: 58 legal homes in 28 shops, all furnished (57 without generated plans; generated plans add 1). 18 of 20 real flats drawn as DXF (rotated, in mm, Catalan layer names) are read back and pass; the other 2 have a back window and are rightly refused.
decision: Keep: every flat furnished and checked; own plans through DXF or JSON; generated plans only when no real plan fits, always marked; the assistant only acts through the page's own tools.

experiment: No more red flats: the generator uses the final inside-the-shop test; smaller flats where the asked ones do not fit
result: 40 real shops: 57 legal homes in 28 shops, every one also passing the Stage 5 check (before: 58 counted, of which 6 crossed the outline and would have failed). 5 shops gain a home. The large demo shop: layouts with 2, 3 and 6 homes, no red flats. The 12 shops left empty have a street front under 6 m (or the deep part under 4 m wide), or are under 6 m deep: a 1,50 m lobby (CTE DB-SUA) plus the narrowest real flat (a 4,7 m studio; 4,44 m of façade for 40 m², Decret 141/2012 3.6.2) does not fit.
decision: Keep: one inside-the-shop test; fill with smaller flats where asked ones do not fit; shops under 6 m of front are reported as too narrow.

experiment: Whole buildings: empty warehouses, commercial and office buildings
result: 4,823 buildings with no homes: 1,741 warehouses, 1,989 commercial, 1,093 office. Of those not in use by the census hint, 893 stand in a zone that admits housing (259 warehouses, 482 commercial, 152 office) and 403 in a zone whose own plan decides. On 40 empty warehouses in zones that admit housing (6 m clear height, mezzanine): 48 homes in 13 buildings, all passing Group B; patios used in 5. Most of the rest are small sheds and garages (50-300 m²). An empty 365 m² nau on Av. Marquès de Castellbell gets 8 homes on 2 levels.
decision: Keep: whole buildings as Group B, mezzanine for tall warehouses, patios only where they light homes, one core per street door. Next: a second exit for deep halls, a real vacancy source, and offices with their own storey heights.

experiment: A second street door for deep buildings; looking for vacancy and height data
result: 67 of the 818 candidate buildings in zones that admit housing (not in use by the census hint) have a part behind a patio on a second street. In 12 tested, the second door adds homes in several: an 903 m² office building 44 -> 55 homes, a 1,073 m² office building 30 -> 40, a 504 m² commercial building 18 -> 24, a 453 m² office building 24 -> 32. The 40-warehouse sample is unchanged (48 homes): those naus have one street.
decision: Keep: a second street door wherever the deep part reaches another street. Vacancy and heights: ask the user (own list, height in step 2) until an official source exists.

experiment: The 29 October crits: real daylight, liveable zones, temporary homes, a city view, the metropolitan area, precedents
result: Real daylight: on 40 real shops, 48 legal homes in 22 shops instead of 57 in 28; 9 homes in 6 shops had rooms mostly in the dark. City: 838 of 1,694 empty shops give 1,405 homes; unused buildings: 249 warehouses give 1,672 homes, 261 commercial buildings 3,414, 211 office buildings 8,077 (several storeys). In zones that admit housing: 6,442 homes; 1,000 homes need 13 places. Avoid: 1,159 not allowed, 949 not liveable, 464 keep it a shop, 739 where no legal home fits. AMB: 201,339 buildings; 15,885 warehouses, commercial and office buildings with no homes; 3,769 in a zone that admits housing, 2,177 where the local plan decides. Shared-space homes: in Barcelona's 40 m² rule they give as many homes as full flats (large demo shop: 6), smaller and with shared rooms.
decision: Keep: real daylight for every place with a prediction, the liveable zones on the plans, shared-space homes as a choice, the city view and the AMB layer. To confirm with the city: the 40 m² reading for shared-space homes and the density exception.

experiment: NOMAD's own plan AI: trained on 15,545 real flats, every plan checked
result: On the 1,496 held-out flats: 70 % of pixels right, mIoU 0,57; 4 % of the drawn plans pass every check with straight walls (23 % with stepped walls, which were rejected). AI library: 227 plans from 5,760 slots. 40 real shops with Bars's daylight: 48 legal homes in 22 shops before; 52 in 25 with the ranking fix; 57 in 28 with the AI plans (36 AI flats used); median floor left unused per shop 134 -> 127 -> 101 m².
decision: Keep: AI plans in the library, marked 'NOMAD AI', only when they pass every check; the ranking fix for all plans. Next: request RPLAN / LIFULL, train longer, and a diffusion model for more variety.
